1) Hold rules: instruct the patient to temporarily stop metformin, lisinopril, and furosemide during any acute illness with vomiting, diarrhea, poor oral intake, significant dizziness/hypotension, decreased urine output, or if told they have dehydration or AKI.  
2) Restart criteria: resume meds only when clinically well, tolerating oral intake, euvolemic, and outpatient labs show creatinine back to within ~20% of baseline and potassium normal; specifically restart metformin only if eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73m2.  
3) OTC cautions: avoid NSAIDs and potassium‑containing salt substitutes, avoid other nephrotoxins, and use acetaminophen for pain unless otherwise directed; follow local protocol to hold metformin around iodinated contrast.  
4) Follow‑up labs: obtain BMP (creatinine, BUN, K+) 48–72 hours after discharge (or immediately if symptoms) and repeat at ~1–2 weeks; arrange PCP or nephrology follow‑up within one week.  
5) Red flags: seek urgent care/ED if new lightheadedness, fainting, markedly decreased urine output, persistent vomiting, or if outpatient labs show a large creatinine rise or K+ >5.5 mmol/L.
